To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel maximum a posteriori (MAP)-based loss function combined with a multi-resolution grid architecture can be applied to a fully automatic 3D cardiac segmentation method which outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning techniques.
we propose an end-to-end, fully automatic method for the segmentation of the cardiac anatomy from MRI volumes.

a deep CNN can be designed to segment all three regions (left ventricular cavity, right ventricular cavity, and left ventricular epicaridum) of a 3-D cardiac MRI volume in 0,4 second with an accuracy comparable to the state-of-the art.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an automatic method for segmenting 3D cardiac MRI images using a novel deep CNN.

the following three aspects: 1) the design and implementation of a novel deep CNN for the segmentation of the left ventricular and right ventricular cavities; 2) the design and evaluation of a novel loss function for cardiac segmentation; 3) the design and training of a novel cardiac center-of-mass regression module for the registration of a shape prior to the cardiac segmentation results.

the following three main contributions: 1) a novel loss function for cardiac segmentation; 2) a novel CNN architecture which learns both low- and high-level features; and 3) a novel CNN which is able to segment all 3 cardiac regions with a single model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method outperforms all other methods in the ACDC challenge.
our method is able to segment all three regions with a high Dice index, in less than a second, and without any manual preprocessing, cropping, or registration.
our method is a fast, fully automatic, robust, and reliable method to segment the heart in a 3D cardiac volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel loss function for the cardiac segmentation problem which is based on the cross-entropy, the predicted contours (with a contour smoothness term), the shape prior (with a center-of-mass regression module), and an a priority term.
we propose a novel CNN for cardiac segmentation that outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning approaches.
we propose a novel deep CNN which can segment the left ventricular and right ventricular cavities as well as the left ventricular wall in 3D MRI images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a novel CNN loss function, a multi-resolution architecture, and an automatic shape prior can significantly improve the segmentation accuracy of deep learning methods.
the proposed network architecture is able to learn both high-level and low-level features from the raw MRI data.
our novel loss function and our conv-deconv ”Grid” architecture allow for a fast and accurate segmentation of the left and right ventricles.
